newsitem.title: Singapore: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in moderate trade on Tuesday, dealers said.

Most traders were sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. June consumer confidence index, which is forecast to show a reading of 126.3 compared with a reading of 127.1 reported in May, they said.

"Rates were quietly steady in the morning except for some position adjustments at the short end. All eyes are on tonight's release of the (U.S. June) consumer confidence index report, for more clues to market direction," a local dealer said.
"But some people are reluctant to open or hold new positions ahead of the outcome of next week's Federal Open Market Committee meeting and June non-farm payrolls report," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Tuesday/Wednesday, Wednesday/Thursday and week-fixed were unchanged from Monday's common 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent, respectively.

Among longer dates, two-months was unchanged from Monday's 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent, four-months unchanged at 5-3/4 5-5/8, six-months unchanged at 5-7/8 5-3/4 and twelve-months unchanged at 6-1/16 5-15/16 percent.
